text:
For most of November, Jacob Fowler has been the reason Montreal games end the way they do. The rookie arrived in Saturday's game at the top of The Hockey News' Calder Trophy tracker. He left it on the wrong end of a 4-3 loss, beaten with 31 seconds to go on a Noah Cates shot that, as Karine Hains of The Hockey News put it, Fowler "can't catch" and dropped in. Sportsnet's Eric Engels summed up the night: "for once, Fowler was human."

The Canadiens had the better of the first period, 0.94 to 0.38 in expected goals (the quality of the chances each team got), and still came out of it tied 1-1 after Oliver Kapanen answered Christian Dvorak's tip-in 16 seconds later. Then Philadelphia took over. Denver Barkey, back in the lineup this week after being cleared to return, scored early in the second and set up Rasmus Ristolainen for a 3-1 lead on a shot our numbers gave a 2% chance. Barkey's case keeps building: PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor wrote after the game that if a more hyped prospect were producing like this in his first full season, "there'd be a ton of excitement around him."

Montreal's push came fast. Lane Hutson drew a penalty on Noel Acciari early in the third, and Zachary Bolduc, working on the second power-play unit, scored from the slot. Owen Beck tied it 74 seconds later, swinging the Canadiens' win chances from 24% to 52%. Hutson finished without a point and still took the third star, which tells you how much of the night ran through him.

The finish belonged to the Flyers' depth line. Cates, set up by Sean Couturier and Matvei Michkov, took a 27% look and Fowler couldn't hold it, a goal that moved Philadelphia's win chances from 48% to 95%. Fowler allowed 1.7 goals more than his 20 shots deserved. Over 60 minutes it was close to a coin flip: our replays gave the Flyers the win 52% of the time.

Philadelphia has now won three straight and swept a two-game road trip. Michkov's name has been all over the trade-rumor headlines for two weeks; on Saturday he was on the ice for the winner. Montreal, already without Chris Kreider for six to eight weeks, will want its rookie goalie back to normal quickly.
headline: Cates wins it late as Fowler's glove fails him
